body:
Makes `FFT2D5MODEL="ORIGINAL"` explicit and restores the solver fixes used to reproduce the published bend benchmark:

- Map particles and the fixed laboratory reference path into the same solve frame; restore particle coordinates and moments after solving or an exception.
- Use the rectangular-cell averaged logarithmic Green function, including its finite self term, and retain the convolution potential halo for centered field differences.
- Reuse one 2D FFT workspace and skip empty slices while clearing their fields. Neutral slices with nonzero charge density remain active.
- Precompute path geometry and project each particle once per solve; reuse the coordinates for coverage, deposition and gathering.
- Accelerate the global nearest-segment search with a per-solve bounding-box hierarchy. Conservative pruning, unchanged segment scoring and lowest-index ties preserve exhaustive-search results; a previous segment only seeds the bound.
- Add opt-in `--2D5BatchSize n`: pack independent transverse slices into contiguous buffers and use existing native heFFTe row executors across slices. Preserve the Green function, normalization and potential halos; no IPPL changes or longitudinal FFT.
- Reduce all local longitudinal-density slices in one team launch and one small host transfer; preserve ghost accumulation, MPI summation and the longitudinal model.
- Parallelize segment/leaf preparation and hierarchy levels while preserving ordered arc lengths, segment scoring and tie handling.
- CPU and A100 validation is described below.

`ORIGINAL` remains the default and only supported model in this PR: independent transverse 2D slices with a local longitudinal closure (`g=6.36` for `PIPEMODE=OPEN`). `PIPEMODE` selects the longitudinal approximation separately. The earlier local `FINITE_SOURCE` model, 3D operators and curvature-correction operators are outside this change.

**Validation:** the normal `TestSpaceChargeConfig`, `TestFFT2D5Algorithm`, `TestFFT2D5Numerics` and `TestPoissonSolver` CTest targets pass with one and four OpenMP threads. Tests cover frame invariance, repeated solves, independent cell-potential quadrature, Gaussian mesh convergence, length-unit scaling and boundary fields. See [unit-test details](https://github.com/OPALX-project/OPALX/blob/574fcabae323dbce9fe247196419b4a2f7d6c95a/unit_tests/SpaceCharge/README.md).

**Test case:** cold protons (β=0.001), a 5 m uniform round bunch with transverse RMS 10 mm, ZeroSC or 10 pC. A uniform vertical magnetic field gives R=2 m. Track 10 m in 100 steps using 1,048,576 common particles and a 512³ charged mesh; compare RMS sizes and emittances with committed 658, PyORBIT and the analytic ZeroSC radial reference.

**Analytic ZeroSC calculation:** exact circular trajectories in the uniform magnetic field give the mean-subtracted radial position–momentum covariance. Moments are integrated over the initial uniform disk, including its curved-volume Jacobian. OPALX samples at common time; PyORBIT samples in s. The plots show the corresponding separate analytic references. Endpoint radial-emittance errors are 0.028% for OPALX and 0.025% for PyORBIT; PyORBIT's maximum absolute curve error is 0.59% of the analytic peak.

![RMS comparison](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OPALX-project/opalx-documents/691d1480bcb27275b8d6b913dd77851f498cb47b/examples/2026/2d5-1/rms.png)

![Emittance comparison with common-time and common-station analytic ZeroSC references](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OPALX-project/opalx-documents/691d1480bcb27275b8d6b913dd77851f498cb47b/examples/2026/2d5-1/emittance.png)

Artifacts are stored in [opalx-documents/examples/2026/2d5-1](https://github.com/OPALX-project/opalx-documents/tree/691d1480bcb27275b8d6b913dd77851f498cb47b/examples/2026/2d5-1).

**100-step, 10 pC inputs:** [OPALX](https://github.com/OPALX-project/opalx-documents/blob/691d1480bcb27275b8d6b913dd77851f498cb47b/examples/2026/2d5-1/inputs/opalx-10pc-100steps.in) · [PyORBIT](https://github.com/OPALX-project/opalx-documents/blob/691d1480bcb27275b8d6b913dd77851f498cb47b/examples/2026/2d5-1/inputs/pyorbit-10pc-100steps.py). [Dependencies and provenance](https://github.com/OPALX-project/opalx-documents/blob/691d1480bcb27275b8d6b913dd77851f498cb47b/examples/2026/2d5-1/inputs/readme.md); external particle and field-map assets are required.

**Performance — same 100-step DBA pilot:** 100,000 matched KV particles, 5.602 nC, 64×64×512 mesh, 3 ps steps, 4 OpenMP threads and one MPI rank. The reference path has 2,606 segments. Use the original transverse slice model with the longitudinal field disabled; all builds are Release.

| Implementation | Elapsed time |
|---|---:|
| Before projection reuse, stock FFT | 73.65 s |
| Reused projections, stock FFT | 51.10 s |
| Reused projections, FFTW 3.3.11 | 32.71 s |
| Exact segment hierarchy, FFTW | 21.27–21.81 s |
| Hierarchy + slice batching (8 or 32), FFTW | **11.02 s** |

The hierarchy reduces projection-kernel time from 10.86 s to 0.396 s (27.4×). Direct tests compare segment indices and all three coordinates **exactly** against an independent exhaustive scan over 43,540 entries, including ties, intersections, repeated vertices, stale seeds, allocation changes and extreme coordinate scales. Hierarchy tracking retains all particles and charge; RMS/emittance differences from the exhaustive FFTW run are ≤1.3×10⁻¹⁴ relative. Full tracking outputs agree at floating-point reduction roundoff, rather than bit-for-bit.

**Slice batching:** `--2D5BatchSize 8` is opt-in; serial remains the default. In the same-executable comparison, batching reduces 21.38 s to about 11.02 s. Sizes 8 and 32 are effectively tied; 8 uses one-quarter the real/spectral buffer memory. With 16 OpenMP threads, batch 8 averaged 12.38 s, slower than with four threads.

New tests compare potential/halo and fields with serial results, covering partial batches, empty/neutral/vacated slices, changed anisotropic grids and open/closed boundaries. Reused OPALX fields now resize through the existing `updateLayout` API. CLI checks and unit tests pass. All pilots retain particle count/charge; RMS/emittance differences are ≤2.3×10⁻¹⁴ relative.

The latest CPU sample is dominated by FFT arithmetic. FFTW threading is available but is **not enabled** by this change. The CPU results above predate CUDA batching and MPI z decomposition. The current validation is below; no 16-turn runs were made.

![Batch-size comparison: means and observed repeat ranges](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OPALX-project/opalx-documents/f2f0cbc56ccfd6edaa0b6c3eb323cbadc10bfcfb/examples/2026/2d5-1/dba-fftw-batching-2026-11-04/2026-11-04-runtime.png)

![Cumulative timings and fresh batch-8 CPU profile](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OPALX-project/opalx-documents/f2f0cbc56ccfd6edaa0b6c3eb323cbadc10bfcfb/examples/2026/2d5-1/dba-fftw-batching-2026-11-04/2026-11-04-profile-with-batch8.png)

[Batching evidence, thread checks and provenance](https://github.com/OPALX-project/opalx-documents/blob/f2f0cbc56ccfd6edaa0b6c3eb323cbadc10bfcfb/examples/2026/2d5-1/dba-fftw-batching-2026-11-04/2026-11-04-readme.md). [Earlier projection/FFTW evidence](https://github.com/OPALX-project/opalx-documents/blob/ce71b018d466eb69d8a247e408b2e2e75194f654/examples/2026/2d5-1/dba-solver-performance-2026-11-04/2026-11-04-readme.md).

Refs #658.


## MPI z decomposition and native GPU row batching

`PARFFTZ=TRUE` distributes complete x–y planes between ranks using the existing OPEN spatial layout and halo exchange. Cartesian particle attributes migrate together through temporary path coordinates and are restored before force evaluation. `--2D5BatchSize 64` groups each rank's local planes. Existing heFFTe R2C/complex row executors transform all x rows across a batch, transpose for the y transforms, multiply by the Green spectrum and reverse the transforms. Plans are reused for full and partial batches. **No IPPL changes, z FFT, curvature correction or 3D solve.** The original longitudinal closure remains separate.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
  R["512 charge slices"] --> A["GPU 0: 256 slices"]
  R --> B["GPU 1: 256 slices"]
  subgraph P["Same independent pipeline on each GPU: four batches of 64"]
    direction LR
    X["Zero-pad x–y planes"] --> F["x R2C → transpose → y FFT"]
    F --> G["Green multiplication"]
    G --> I["inverse y → transpose back → x C2R"]
    I --> E["Potential gradient: Ex, Ey"]
  end
  A --> X
  B --> X
  R --> L["One batched density launch → small MPI reduction → gradient: Ez"]
  E --> H["Halo exchange and particle gather"]
  L --> H
```

**Matched before/after pilot:** 100 steps, 100,000 particles, 5.602 nC, 64×64×512, dt=3 ps and batch 64. Both executables use `PIPEMODE="OPEN"`, enabling longitudinal fields. CPU: Release FFTW, one OpenMP thread per rank. GPU: one A100 per MPI rank.

| Configuration | Previous SC [ms/call] | Row-batched SC [ms/call] | Speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 CPU rank | 98.01 | 81.79 | 1.20× |
| 2 CPU ranks | 65.30 | 51.92 | 1.26× |
| 1 A100 | 89.24 | 19.02 | 4.69× |
| 2 A100s | 50.71 | 15.37 | 3.30× |

SC averages cover the 99 steady physical solves; initialization, zero-source warmup and the first physical solve are timed separately. These are **space-charge timings, not complete process times**. The one-A100 Poisson stage falls from 72.88 to 2.32 ms/call over all 100 calls. Whole-Poisson two-GPU scaling is limited in this pilot; full process times and first-call costs are in the report.

Before/after RMS/emittance differences are ≤1.5×10⁻¹⁴ relative; particle positions differ by ≤3.84×10⁻¹³ m. 

![Current CPU/A100 timings](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OPALX-project/opalx-documents/4f48754ce509567decfdb9bb058facde1c6dfa69/examples/2026/2d5-1/r2c-row-integration-2026-11-06/timing-comparison.png)

[Architecture, full timings, limits and reproducible analysis](https://github.com/OPALX-project/opalx-documents/blob/4f48754ce509567decfdb9bb058facde1c6dfa69/examples/2026/2d5-1/r2c-row-integration-2026-11-06/readme.md) · [heFFTe interface microbenchmark](https://github.com/OPALX-project/opalx-documents/blob/4f48754ce509567decfdb9bb058facde1c6dfa69/examples/2026/2d5-1/heffte-batch-microbenchmark-2026-11-06/readme.md). Raw particle snapshots and executables stay at the recorded run locations and are not committed. No 16-turn runs.


### Batched longitudinal density

Replace one synchronized reduction per z slice with one team launch for all local planes and one small host transfer. Ordered ghost accumulation, MPI summation, boundary conditions and the original longitudinal closure are unchanged. Nsight confirms **100 density kernels instead of 51,200** for the one-GPU 100-step pilot.

Fresh baseline and optimized builds use the same source base (`57f399729`), the OPEN pilot above and unchanged executables within each comparison:

| Configuration | Density before → after [ms/call] | Steady SC before → after [ms/call] |
|---|---:|---:|
| 1 CPU rank | 2.452 → 1.684 | 78.320 → 77.012 |
| 2 CPU ranks | 1.167 → 0.769 | 51.686 → 51.059 |
| 1 A100 | 12.141 → **0.145** | 19.634 → **7.774** |
| 2 A100s | 5.942 → **0.168** | 15.366 → **9.892** |
| 3 A100s | 4.144 → **0.167** | 13.557 → **9.580** |

Before/after RMS and emittance differences are <4×10⁻¹⁴ relative; all particle IDs and charge are preserved. Tolerances are unchanged.

![Density-batching timings](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OPALX-project/opalx-documents/4afaf396d919e4091d53e1736faff902e4696a12/examples/2026/2d5-1/longitudinal-density-batch-2026-11-06/density-timing.png)

**Density-only complete-tracking estimate (before geometry parallelization):** unprofiled 100/1,000-step calibration gives 13.416, 14.069 and 14.127 ms/step on 1/2/3 A100s: approximately **1 h 28 min / 1 h 32 min / 1 h 33 min per turn** at 3 ps. 

[Results, executable identities, limits and reproducible analysis](https://github.com/OPALX-project/opalx-documents/blob/4afaf396d919e4091d53e1736faff902e4696a12/examples/2026/2d5-1/longitudinal-density-batch-2026-11-06/readme.md). Particle snapshots and raw traces remain at native run locations. [Earlier GPU profile](https://github.com/OPALX-project/opalx-documents/blob/7686182ec3bd26f5e8206c8f4b9ec4546a8eab2b/examples/2026/2d5-1/row-batching-profile-2026-11-06/readme.md) predates this density optimization.
### Parallel geometry/hierarchy — latest results

Build segments and endpoint boxes in parallel, then merge tree levels within one GPU team. Arc lengths retain their original addition order; hierarchy topology, segment scoring, pruning and ties are unchanged. No IPPL changes.

Same OPEN 100-step DBA pilot, batch 64; paired preserved/new executables:

| A100s | Geometry kernels before → after [ms/step] | Steady SC before → after [ms/call] | Total process before → after [s] |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 4.044 → **0.254** | 7.666 → **3.876** | 8.84 → **8.36** |
| 2 | 4.070 → **0.260** | 9.723 → **5.948** | 11.37 → **10.90** |

The build is about **16× faster**. Exact geometry, bounding-box, segment-index and projection checks pass on CPU and CUDA. CPU checks cover 1/4 OpenMP threads and 1/2/4 MPI ranks; GPU field checks cover 1/2 ranks. Full tracking agrees at roundoff (<2.3×10⁻¹⁴ relative RMS/emittance differences), rather than bitwise. All particles and charge are preserved.

![Latest geometry and tracking timings](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OPALX-project/opalx-documents/7825136a5b9eae9ee37bba8f7f450045acc0143e/examples/2026/2d5-1/parallel-geometry-gpu-2026-11-06/timings.png)

**Updated one-turn estimate: 63.1 min on one A100; 67.5 min on two.** Subtract the measured steady-SC saving from the earlier 100/1,000-step complete-tracking calibration, assuming unchanged non-SC work. This is an extrapolation, not a fresh calibration or completed turn. One GPU remains fastest; about 5% further improvement is needed for one hour. The three-A100 job was cancelled before starting. No full-turn or 16-turn runs.

**Current one-A100 runtime distribution:** coordinate transformations account for 37% of GPU kernel time, beam moments 25%, Poisson grid kernels 14%, FFT arithmetic 6%, and geometry/hierarchy 4%. The existing trace shows about 731 kernel executions and 397 synchronization calls per step. Kernels are active for 48% of the cropped profiled window; this measures temporal activity, not SM occupancy. CUDA API durations overlap GPU execution. No extra simulation was needed for this breakdown.

![Current one-A100 runtime distribution](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OPALX-project/opalx-documents/7825136a5b9eae9ee37bba8f7f450045acc0143e/examples/2026/2d5-1/parallel-geometry-gpu-2026-11-06/runtime-breakdown.png)

[GPU results, profile method and turn-estimate calculation](https://github.com/OPALX-project/opalx-documents/blob/7825136a5b9eae9ee37bba8f7f450045acc0143e/examples/2026/2d5-1/parallel-geometry-gpu-2026-11-06/readme.md) · [CPU checks and timing plots](https://github.com/OPALX-project/opalx-documents/blob/7825136a5b9eae9ee37bba8f7f450045acc0143e/examples/2026/2d5-1/parallel-geometry-cpu-2026-11-06/readme.md). Timers distinguish GPU execution, steady SC and startup-inclusive process time. Raw particles/traces and previous executables remain at their run locations.

### Cleanup and CPU/GPU revalidation

Remove the IPPL comparison backend and unused code, split long solve methods into documented stage helpers, and right-size the MPI Green workspace. No IPPL library, physics model or numerical tolerance changes.

Focused CPU tests pass with 1/4 OpenMP threads and two MPI ranks. CUDA algorithm/numerical tests and one/two-rank parallel tests pass. Paired preserved/new executables run the same OPEN 100-step DBA pilot above, including longitudinal fields. All 100,000 particles and charge are preserved; maximum rms/emittance differences are **1.69×10⁻¹⁴ on CPU** and **1.35×10⁻¹⁴ on GPU**, consistent with reduction roundoff.

| Configuration | Process before → after [s] | Steady SC before → after [ms/call] |
|---|---:|---:|
| 1 CPU rank, 1 OMP thread | 16.280 → 16.153 | 79.972 → 79.777 |
| 2 CPU ranks, 1 OMP thread/rank | 8.962 → 8.874 | 51.407 → 50.687 |
| 1 A100 | 8.367 → 8.474 | 3.924 → 3.902 |
| 2 A100s | 10.959 → 10.797 | 5.882 → 5.819 |

Steady SC covers 99 solves, excluding initialization, warmup and the first physical solve. One pair per configuration; timing is essentially unchanged. Previous executables and raw runs are retained. No 16-turn runs.

![Cleanup: CPU timings](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OPALX-project/opalx-documents/7ee66b7fe9d1cc4811891ddb045ef44d4e43bac1/examples/2026/2d5-1/cleanup-2026-11-07/timings.png)

![Cleanup: A100 timings](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OPALX-project/opalx-documents/7ee66b7fe9d1cc4811891ddb045ef44d4e43bac1/examples/2026/2d5-1/cleanup-2026-11-07/gpu-timings.png)

[Validation, timing breakdown and provenance](https://github.com/OPALX-project/opalx-documents/blob/7ee66b7fe9d1cc4811891ddb045ef44d4e43bac1/examples/2026/2d5-1/cleanup-2026-11-07/readme.md).

commits.messageHeadline: Make original FFT2D5 model selection explicit
Update ORIGINAL benchmarks and distinguish ZeroSC sampling conventions
Attach OPALX and PyORBIT inputs for 100-step charged benchmark
Move FFT2D5 benchmark artifacts to opalx-documents

commits.messageBody:
Map particles and the laboratory reference path into a shared solve frame,
restoring coordinates and moments on success or failure. Integrate the 2D
logarithmic Green function over each source cell and retain the convolution
potential halo for centered boundary fields.

Reuse one slice solver workspace and skip exactly empty density slices while
clearing stale fields. Keep nonzero neutral sources active.

Bring the matching frame and independent numerical unit tests into the normal
CTest targets. Preserve the explicit ORIGINAL model selection and document the
checks. The solver/test changes are carried over from fd6ba8dc5; no experimental
finite-source or curvature operator is included.

Validation: configuration, algorithm and numerics CTest targets pass with 1 and
4 OpenMP threads; the two-rank unsupported-configuration rejection test passes.
The source matches the build used for the published benchmark repeat.
commits.messageHeadline: Fix FFT2D5 frames, transverse cell fields and workspace reuse

commits.messageBody:
Precompute segment geometry and cumulative path lengths in one preparation
call, then project each active particle once. Reuse the projections for
coverage checking, charge deposition and field gathering.

Refresh caches on every solve and resize buffers when particle counts change.
Keep standalone diagnostic stages uncached. Preserve the existing search
order, clamping and nearest-segment tie handling.

Add detailed Doxygen documentation and unit checks against the uncached
stages, covering density, E/B fields, seams, invalid particles and source
changes.

Validation:
- Normal unit targets pass with 1 and 4 OpenMP threads.
- Unsupported two-rank execution is still rejected.
- Identical 100-step pilot runtime drops from 73.65 s to 50.78–54.85 s.
- RMS/emittance differences remain below 1.75e-14 relative.
- Original executable preserved; no 16-turn runs started.
commits.messageHeadline: Cache FFT2D5 path geometry and reuse projections within each solve

commits.messageBody:
Build a per-solve hierarchy of segment bounding boxes and seed its search
with the previous segment. Use conservative floating-point pruning and
lowest-index tie handling, with an exhaustive fallback for stack exhaustion.

Compare segment indices and projected coordinates exactly with an independent
exhaustive scan, including intersections, ties, stale seeds and extreme scales.
Document the search, cache lifetime, numerical guard and memory cost.

Validation: four unit targets pass with one and four OpenMP threads; the
unsupported two-rank check passes. The unchanged 100-step DBA pilot drops
from 32.71 s to 21.27–21.81 s. Projection time falls from 10.86 s to 0.396 s;
tracking differences remain at floating-point reduction roundoff.
commits.messageHeadline: Accelerate FFT2D5 nearest-segment search without changing projections

commits.messageBody:
Add --2D5BatchSize as an explicit positive-integer option, retaining serial
slice execution by default. Reuse native heFFTe R2C batch calls and contiguous
buffers without changing IPPL or transforming the longitudinal direction.
Preserve the existing Green function, normalization, potential halo and field
differences; keep diagnostic callbacks on the serial path.

Resize reused OPALX fields through updateLayout when the transverse grid
changes. Test partial batches, empty/neutral/vacated slices, anisotropic grids,
potential halos, unchanged sources and complete solves under both boundary modes.

Validation: four unit targets pass with one and four OpenMP threads, ten CLI
checks pass, and two-rank execution remains rejected. The identical 100-step
pilot drops from 21.38 s to about 11.02 s for batch sizes 8 and 32, with
RMS/emittance differences below 2.2e-14 relative. Host execution only; no
16-turn runs.
commits.messageHeadline: Batch independent FFT2D5 slice transforms within OPALX

commits.messageBody:
Recognize --input filename when deciding whether --restart has an optional
checkpoint argument. This avoids treating the checkpoint as another input
file when the explicit input option follows it.

Validated restart/input ordering with and without --2D5BatchSize using the
current Release/OpenMP build.
commits.messageHeadline: Fix restart look-ahead for explicit input files

commits.messageBody:
Replace the invalid deterministic 5.5-sigma maximum assertion with a
binomial tail-count check using the analytic normal probability and a
Bernstein/union bound. Keep the RMS tolerances and finite z cutoff, and
check finiteness in all six coordinates.

All eight Gaussian cases pass five repeats at 1, 4 and 16 OpenMP threads,
and two-rank runs at 1 and 4 threads. A temporary 3-sigma clipping negative
control is rejected by the new assertions.
commits.messageHeadline: Test untruncated Gaussian tails statistically

commits.messageBody:
Use the existing native-memory heFFTe batch path on CUDA and enable batch numerical checks for device fields. Document buffer residency, synchronization and backend batching limits. Move the exhaustive projection oracle outside the private GoogleTest body so NVCC can compile it without changing its calculations.

Validated on one A100 with the matched 100-step DBA pilot at batch sizes 1, 8, 32 and 64. Batch 64 halves tracking time, reduces kernel launches by 52.8% and device synchronizations by 82.9%, with moments agreeing to roundoff. GPU numerical and local OpenMP tests pass; the previously observed CUDA algorithm-test launch crash remains under investigation.
commits.messageHeadline: Enable FFT2D5 slice batching on CUDA

commits.messageBody:
Replace the remaining extended lambda in the diagnostic-policy header template with a named functor. This avoids a null NVCC lambda-copy helper when the library and test translation units instantiate the same kernel, preserving the scan and atomic marking exactly.

All five checked A100 test targets pass, including all eleven FFT2D5 algorithm tests. OpenMP tests pass with one and four threads. Serial and batch64 pilots, the longitudinal charged bend and a complete 393240-step DBA reference run pass completion checks without changing IPPL or numerical tolerances.
commits.messageHeadline: Fix CUDA launch of FFT2D5 slice occupancy kernel
Merge branch 'master' into codex/fft2d5-explicit-original-model

commits.messageBody:
Reuse OPEN spatial migration and halo exchange for complete transverse planes per rank. Batch x rows and transposed y columns through existing heFFTe executors without IPPL changes; retain potential halos and normalized Green scaling.

Separate initialization, zero-source warmup, first physical solve and synchronized steady timers. Add distributed direct-convolution and partial-batch equivalence coverage plus a standalone backend microbenchmark. CPU and one/two-A100 100-step pilots retain RMS/emittances to roundoff with longitudinal fields enabled.
commits.messageHeadline: Parallelize FFT2D5 z slabs and batch native R2C row transforms
Merge remote-tracking branch 'origin/codex/fft2d5-explicit-original-m…

commits.messageBody:
Replace synchronized per-slice reductions with one team launch and one small profile transfer. Preserve ordered ghost accumulation, MPI summation, boundary handling and the longitudinal model.

Add independent host-sum coverage for density and gradients, tiny periodic slabs, empty reuse and unchanged charge storage. Validated CPU and one-, two- and three-A100 pilots without tolerance changes.
commits.messageHeadline: Batch FFT2D5 longitudinal density reductions across local slices

commits.messageBody:
Build independent segments and leaf boxes across the device, then merge hierarchy levels within one team. Preserve increasing-index arc-length summation and the existing nearest-segment search without changing IPPL.

Check geometry entries and bounding boxes exactly against the previous serial device build, alongside the exhaustive projection oracle. Validate CPU OpenMP/MPI and A100 pilots without changing numerical tolerances.

Apply clang-format 21.1.8 to FFT2D5 changes

title: Fix and accelerate the original FFT2D5 solver
